c.tagline: Ancient Serdica meets Balkan mountains and Soviet-era grandeur.

taxi.fareNote: Meters required by law; confirm the driver starts it. Use reputable apps (Bolt/Yango) or licensed companies (OK Supertrans, Green Taxi) to avoid overcharging at tourist spots and the airport.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide single emergency number and works for all services (police, fire, ambulance) throughout Bulgaria.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing on transit; taxi scams — use registered cabs/apps

hood_desc: The historic core around Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, Serdika ruins, and the Largo, packed with museums, churches and government buildings - best for first-time visitors who want everything walkable.
Sofia's premier pedestrian shopping and dining artery lined with cafes, boutiques and Mount Vitosha views - ideal for travelers who want to be in the middle of the action.

The area around the National Palace of Culture (NDK) and South Park's edge, quieter and leafy but still central - suits business travelers and those wanting easy metro access without the tourist crowds.
A trendy, youthful residential district near South Park full of restaurants, craft-beer bars and coworking cafes - popular with digital nomads and younger travelers.
An elegant, tree-lined embassy district near the Cathedral with grand early-20th-century architecture - good for travelers wanting upscale calm close to the sights.

water.note: Tap water meets EU standards and is generally safe to drink.

transit.pay: Buy paper tickets from kiosks or drivers, or use rechargeable contactless cards for metro/tram/bus, tapped at metro turnstiles or validated onboard surface vehicles. Mobile ticketing apps (e.g. mCard/Sofia Traffic app) are also accepted.
transit.hours: Metro runs roughly 05:00-00:00; surface transport similar hours with reduced night bus coverage.
transit.note: Single ride ~1.03 USD (1.60 BGN); day passes and multi-ride cards offer savings for longer stays.

train: Central Railway Station Sofia, connections to Plovdiv, Varna, Burgas, Istanbul, Belgrade, Bucharest

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving 5-10% in restaurants is appreciated but not mandatory; not customary for taxis.

places.name: Divaka

food.name: Rakia

landmarks: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral
This monumental gold-domed Neo-Byzantine cathedral, built to honor Russian soldiers, is Sofia's grandest landmark and the most photographed building in Bulgaria.
Church of St Sofia
A humble 6th-century red-brick basilica that gave the city its name, standing quietly beside its far grander neighbor as a testament to Sofia's ancient roots.
Rotunda of Saint George
A red-brick Roman rotunda from the 4th century, the oldest building in Sofia, tucked incongruously among Communist-era buildings and Roman ruins.
Banya Bashi Mosque
This 16th-century Ottoman mosque with its soaring minaret and domed roof remains an active place of worship and a striking reminder of Sofia's layered history.
Sofia Synagogue
One of Europe's largest synagogues, this Moorish Revival masterpiece dazzles with an enormous brass chandelier and ornate domed sanctuary.
National Palace of Culture (NDK)
A vast Communist-era cultural complex fronted by a sweeping plaza and fountains, symbolizing Sofia's modern skyline against the Vitosha mountain backdrop.
Vitosha Boulevard
Sofia's pedestrian shopping street, lined with cafes, boutiques, and views of Vitosha mountain, buzzing with locals and visitors alike day and night.
Ivan Vazov National Theatre
Bulgaria's grandest theatre, a neoclassical building with columned facade and sculpted pediment, framed beautifully by its fountain-filled garden square.
Vitosha Mountain
Rising dramatically over the capital, this accessible mountain offers hiking, skiing, and sweeping panoramic views of the entire city below.
Central Sofia Market Hall
An Art Nouveau covered market from 1911 with an ornate clock-topped facade, still bustling with vendors selling local produce and goods.

train.note: The Sofia-Istanbul Express is a nightly sleeper; bring your passport for the border stop. The Bucharest day train runs direct roughly mid-June to early October (change at Ruse the rest of the year) and currently leaves from Sofia Sever station due to track works. Trains to Belgrade and Thessaloniki remain suspended.

bus.note: Most international coaches leave from Sofia Central Bus Station (Serdika), next to the railway station. Buses are the practical option for Belgrade, Skopje and Thessaloniki while those train routes are suspended.

ferry.note: Sofia is inland with no ferry links. Bulgaria has no regular international passenger ferries; the Black Sea coast (Varna, Burgas) is served by trains and buses instead.
